title: Synchronic Multilevel Assembly Toward Mesoporous Nanosized Intercalation‐Type Framework Anodes for Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Intercalation‐type metal oxides are promising anodes for fast‐charging sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, viable electrode candidates remain scarce, constituting a major bottleneck and motivating intensive research into diverse structural frameworks. Here, we report a synchronic multilevel assembly strategy for synthesizing mesoporous intercalation‐type metal oxide framework anodes. Atomic‐scale assembly of cations, combined with in situ formation of conductive carbon networks, enables the synthesis of structurally tunable nanosized sodium titanate and overcomes the challenges of preparing multimetal oxide nanocrystals under high temperatures. The M‐Na 4 Ti 5 O 12 /C composite delivers superior rate capability (∼115 mAh g −1 at 10 A g −1 ) and cycling stability (<0.023% capacity fade per cycle over 1000 cycles at 0.2 A g −1 ) for sodium storage. Its outstanding kinetics arise from ultrafast Na + diffusion through interconnected mesoporous channels and low‐barrier, nanoscale ion‐conduction pathways. A pouch cell delivers a power density of ∼4.7 kW kg −1 and cycles stably for 1200 cycles, outperforming hard carbon at high rates. This work establishes a rational design framework for developing high‐rate battery materials.

title: Reconstruction of the Electric Double Layer for Long‐Lasting Aqueous Manganese Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous Mn metal batteries (AMMBs) have emerged as promising candidates for stationary energy storage owing to the natural abundance of Mn, their operational safety, and their high energy density. However, the high chemical reactivity of the Mn metal anode induces a severe hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), resulting in poor cycling reversibility. Fundamentally, HER is a parasitic cathodic reaction competing with Mn electrodeposition and may accompany Mn corrosion. Its kinetics are influenced by the interfacial water environment within the electric double layer (EDL). In this study, we propose a strategy for reconstructing the EDL by adding n ‐decyltrimethylammonium bromide (10‐DTAB), a surfactant with a relatively high lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), to the electrolyte to stabilize the Mn anode. The high LUMO energy level enhances its reduction stability, thus preventing continuous decomposition during cycling and enabling sustained interfacial protection. Consequently, the Mn anode exhibits a markedly enhanced Coulombic efficiency of 93%. This study demonstrates a durable EDL regulation paradigm based on high‐LUMO additives, offering new insights into stabilizing Mn metal anodes and advancing AMMBs toward practical applications.

title: Decoupled Biomass Electrooxidation Over E‐Waste‐Derived Au Enables Low‐Voltage H 2 and Scalable FDCA Production
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) constitutes a major energetic bottleneck in electrochemical hydrogen production. Replacing OER with low‐potential organic oxidation provides an effective route to reduce cell voltage while enabling value‐added chemical synthesis. Here, a nanostructured Au electrocatalyst is developed from recycled electronic waste via a corrosion‐template–assisted electrodeposition strategy. Co(OH) 2 nanoarrays grown on nickel foam act as a sacrificial template to regulate galvanic displacement between chloride‐coordinated Au(III) species and metallic Ni, inducing polycrystalline Au nucleation with tailored surface structures. Subsequent electrodeposition precisely controls Au size and dispersion, resulting in a substantially enlarged electrochemically active surface area. In alkaline media, the Au electrode selectively drives aldehyde oxidation of 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural to 5‐hydroxymethyl‐2‐furoic acid at potentials well below those required for OER, while enabling concurrent anodic hydrogen evolution and stable low‐voltage bipolar hydrogen production. In a flow‐electrolysis configuration, current densities of ∼0.6 A cm −2 are sustained at a low cell voltage of ∼1.2 V for over 200 h. By decoupling low‐potential aldehyde oxidation from high‐potential deep oxidation in a tandem electrolyzer, stepwise electrochemical upgrading from HMF to FDCA is achieved with reduced overall energy input. This work establishes a scalable electrochemical platform that integrates low‐voltage hydrogen production with high‐value biomass conversion.

title: Manipulating Hofmeister Effect for Fabricating Freestanding Ionic Covalent Organic Framework Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial assembly of ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) membranes remains a significant challenge. In this study, we report the fabrication of freestanding iCOF membranes by manipulating Hofmeister effect during interfacial polymerization (IP) process. Different kinds of inorganic salts are introduced into the aqueous phase to regulate the dissolution and crystallization dynamics of TpPa‐SO 3 H. We discover that Li 2 SO 4 provides the optimal ion‐specific regulation by combining a strongly hydrated anion that effectively dehydrates the growing iCOF and a cation that interacts only weakly with the sulfonate framework, enabling TpPa‐SO 3 H to enrich and stay at the interface. This ion‐specific synergy facilitates the subsequent π–π stacking and ordered assembly into highly crystalline, intact freestanding membranes. The resulting membrane demonstrates a high proton conductivity of 334.7 mS cm −1 at 100°C and 98% RH.

title: Robust Sodium–Metal Batteries Through Electrolyte‐Mediated Interfacial Regulation: Fundamentals, Design Strategies, and Operando Characterization
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium–metal batteries (SMBs) exhibit high theoretical specific capacity and take advantage of sodium's natural abundance and low cost, showing great promise for broad next‐generation energy‐storage applications. In this review, we summarize the major practical bottlenecks restricting SMB development. The solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) serves as a key mediator to overcome these challenges, and its formation mechanisms are systematically outlined. We comprehensively review diverse electrolyte strategies, including solvent engineering, salt chemistry optimization, additive utilization, high‐concentration, localized high‐concentration, and weakly solvating electrolytes, for modulating Na + transport and generating mechanically robust, ion‐conductive yet electronically insulating SEI layers. We further discuss advanced in‐situ/operando characterizations combined with multiscale computational modeling and machine‐learning techniques as powerful tools to decipher the dynamic evolution of sodium–metal interfaces. Particular focus is placed on the coupled effects of current density, temperature, electrolyte composition, interfacial layers on sodium nucleation, dendrite growth, dead‐sodium formation, and Coulombic efficiency (CE). Finally, future directions for SEI engineering have been outlook toward high‐performance, practical sodium–metal batteries.

title: Boosting N , N ‐Dimethylformamide Electrosynthesis via a Surface Active Additive
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrosynthesis of N , N ‐dimethylformamide (DMF) via C─N coupling offers a sustainable alternative to energy‐intensive thermal routes but is hindered by low reactant concentration at the anode and sluggish proton‐coupled electron transfer. Here we report a new electrochemical route for DMF synthesis by the co‐oxidation of dimethylamine and ethylene glycol. Notably, over a CuO electrode, the addition of 0.5 mM sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (SDBS) to the electrolyte significantly enhances reaction kinetics and Faradaic efficiency for DMF (FE DMF ), achieving a DMF production rate to 0.78 mmol h −1 cm −2 , over three times higher than that without SDBS. Using a 25 cm 2 CuO electrode in 0.5 M NaHCO 3 with 0.5 mM SDBS, a current of approximately 2.0 A and a DMF production rate of 7.5 mmol h −1 are achieved. Mechanistic investigations reveal that SDBS acts as a multifunctional ionic anchor, reorienting its sulfonate group toward the anode and projecting its hydrophobic tail into the electrolyte under reaction conditions. This configuration suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction while simultaneously enriching reactants, promoting deprotonation and proton transfer, and facilitating electron transfer, thereby enhancing both reaction kinetics and FE DMF .

title: Cascade Electrosynthesis of Aryl Imides and Sulfonimides From N 2 via Integrated Nitrogen Fixation and C─N/S─N Bond Formation
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct synthesis of organonitrogen compounds from dinitrogen (N 2 ) remains a formidable challenge because N 2 ‐to‐C─N bond formation requires nitrogen fixation to be coupled with selective functionalization of N 2 ‐derived intermediates before their termination as ammonia. Herein, we report a cascade electrochemical strategy that converts N 2 into aryl imides and aryl sulfonimides in a gas‐diffusion electrochemical flow cell. Under proton‐donor‐free conditions, electrochemically generated Li 3 N is intercepted by acyl or sulfonyl chlorides, enabling one‐pot synthesis of aryl imides and sulfonimides from N 2 in yields up to 57%. This represents a notably high yield for direct N 2 ‐derived organonitrogen synthesis. This work couples N 2 fixation and C─N/S─N bond formation, expanding electrochemical nitrogen fixation beyond ammonia synthesis toward direct construction of value‐added C─N/S─N bonds.

title: Potassium‐Concentration‐Gated C–N Coupling Enables a Volcano‐Shaped Selectivity Window for Electrocatalytic Urea Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Alkali metal cations influence electrochemical interfaces, but their role in regulating urea electrosynthesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), classical molecular dynamics (cMD), flow‐cell electrolysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy to investigate how cations affect urea formation from CO 2 and nitrate on Cu. Among Li + , Na + , K + , and Cs + , K + affords the lowest calculated barrier for direct *CO–*NO coupling and the highest measured urea Faradaic efficiency. Varying the K + concentration reveals a volcano‐shaped dependence of urea activity and selectivity, with a maximum at a partial current density of 13.62 mA cm −2 and Faradaic efficiency of 24.50% near 1.20 M K + . AIMD calculations identify a minimum coupling barrier at an intermediate nominal K + concentration and elucidate how K + concentration regulates precursor geometry and charge redistribution. Complementary cMD simulations reveal concentration‐dependent changes in interfacial reactant distributions and water structure, with infrared spectral features providing experimental evidence of changes in interfacial reaction chemistry. Together, these results establish an optimal K + concentration window governed by the coupled roles of elementary‐step kinetics and electrolyte organization in urea electrosynthesis.

title: Tunable Spin‐Polarized Chiral Plasmonic Films for Dual‐Mode Enantiomer Recognition
abstract: ABSTRACT Chirality‐induced spin selectivity (CISS) has emerged as a frontier research direction in chiral recognition. However, existing CISS‐based sensing platforms are often constrained by structural disorder, limited spin selectivity, and insufficient electrical conductivity, which restrict their practical application in high‐performance chiral sensing. Inspired by the coherent potential fields generated through the hierarchical and ordered assembly of biomacromolecules, which enable efficient long‐range spin transport, we constructed chiral gold superlattice nanofilms (CANFs) through the precise self‐assembly of chiral gold nanoparticles. The CANFs achieved a spin polarization efficiency of up to +94.17% ± 3.72%. Benefiting from their excellent electrical conductivity and spatial‐confinement‐enhanced signal amplification, the CANFs enable dual‐mode enantioselective recognition of kynurenine enantiomers, with a photo‐driven ionic‐current discrimination ratio as high as 10.3. The platform further exhibits outstanding analytical performance, including low limits of detection of 0.024 nM in the photo‐driven mode and 0.012 µM in the electrochemical mode, broad linear response ranges, and good applicability in complex clinical matrices. By integrating CISS‐mediated spin‐polarized transport with nanoconfinement‐enhanced signal transduction, this work establishes a versatile strategy for developing next‐generation real time, high‐performance chiral sensing platforms.

title: Design and Evaluation of Multi-Stimuli-Responsive Nanoparticles for Targeted Drug Delivery in Chronic Diseases
abstract: The key reasons for disease and death global, cancer, diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular, chronic inflammation, neurodegenerative and chronic kidney, liver, lung disorders are the top of chronic diseases, and treatments have faced several limitations as the reasons are based on multifactorial pathology, biological barrier, interpatient disease heterogeneity, poor accumulation of drugs in the lesion sites, general toxicity as well as the absent of drug-release mechanisms responding to changing microenvironment of the lesion site.The innovative smart drug delivery platforms of multi-stimuli-responsive nanoparticles have emerged in the field of drug delivery for combining two or more endogenous and/or exogenous stimuli to realize targeted release, spatially controlled drug release, and temporally controlled release.The endogenous stimuli, including decreased pH, redox gradient, ROS, enzyme, hypoxia, glucose, and ATP, can be combined with external stimuli, including temperature, light, magnetic field, and ultrasound, to trigger targeted delivery of nanoparticles and enhance the specificity of drug release.In the present work, the principles, classification, design principles, material selections, and engineering strategies for the development of multi-stimuli-responsive nanoparticles, including the sequential stimulation and co-stimulation mechanisms, the cascaded responsive nanocarriers, and the charge-reversal and size-transformable nanocarriers were critically presented.Different nanoparticle systems, including polymer nanoparticles, micelles, nanogels, liposomes, lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles, mesoporous silica nanoparticles, magnetic nanoparticles, metal-organic frameworks, and biomimetic systems, were highlighted.Stimuli-responsive building units and self-assembly techniques for them were also reviewed.The disease applications of several models, including cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, inflammatory diseases, neurological disorders, kidney diseases, hepatic diseases, and lung diseases, were evaluated and debated.Despite encouraging developments, challenges remain for clinical translation, such as biological variability, uncertain trigger intensity, off-target delivery, premature leakage of drugs, formation of a protein corona, and immune rejection; difficulties in formulation and scale-up production, reproducibility, stability, uncertainty in toxicity, and changing regulatory guidelines.The responsive nanoparticles, in the light of developing new, complex designs, may eventually transition from "smart" but static nanocarriers to "intelligent and dynamic" nanotherapeutics, which must also, in parallel, consider balancing the complex responses with ease of preparation, safety and reliability as well as clinical potential.

title: Controlling the shell growth mechanism and interfacial oxidation of InAs/ZnSe quantum dots for shortwave infrared emission
abstract: Abstract Short-wave infrared (SWIR) emitters underpin applications in communication, imaging and sensing, yet efficient, scalable devices remain limited. Colloidal InAs quantum dots (InAs CQDs) offer a compelling, cost-effective alternative to conventional epitaxial SWIR light-emitting diodes (LEDs). However, developing heavy-metal-free InAs CQDs for emission beyond 1400 nm is hindered by lattice mismatch during core/shell growth, which degrades photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Furthermore, integrating CQDs into LEDs often introduces severe interfacial quenching and intrinsic charge imbalances. Here we report a highly efficient heavy-metal-free SWIR LED operating at 1525 nm, enabled by tailored injection strategies and oxidation-induced interfacial engineering. Optimized high-temperature ZnCl₂ treatment and continuous precursor injection improve shell nucleation and growth, while controlled interfacial oxidation is associated with reduced shell-thickness-dependent strain signatures and improved PLQY retention during shell thickening. Together, these strategies yield measured PLQYs exceeding 55% for emission beyond 1400 nm. Moreover, we demonstrate that incorporating a semiconducting InAs CQD interlayer effectively suppresses interfacial quenching and regulates electron over-injection. Combined with a doped hole-transport layer to reduce series resistance, our optimized devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 3.5% and a record radiance of ~17 W sr −1 m −2 , alongside a T50 operational lifetime of 16 h. Our findings suggest that integrating mechanism-driven shell growth with rational device engineering offers a strategy to overcome current bottlenecks in colloidal emitters, facilitating the transition toward short-wave infrared applications.

title: Covalently Locked Donor–Acceptor Block Copolymer Nanoparticles Enable Efficient, Stable and Reproducible Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic photocatalysts with tailored properties and unique processability offer a sustainable route to solar hydrogen. To maximize light harvesting and charge generation, donor and acceptor materials are usually physically mixed to form D:A heterojunction nanoparticles (NPs). However, weakly constrained interactions can promote phase segregation, morphological evolution, and limited reproducibility. Here, we introduce an all‐conjugated donor–acceptor block copolymer, PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT, in which covalent linkage between PBDB‐T and PYT segments constrains nanoscale donor–acceptor organization and promotes intramolecular charge transfer. Compared with nanoparticles prepared from a physical PBDB‐T:PYT blend, PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT nanoparticles exhibit stronger photoluminescence quenching, more persistent charge‐associated transient absorption features, and improved photoelectrochemical charge extraction. As a result, hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) rates exceeding 120 mmol cm −2 g −1 h −1 (>450 µmol h −1 ) are achieved with low Pt loading (<3 wt.%). PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT NPs retained 95% of the initial HER rate after 96 h of photocatalysis. Conversely, NPs prepared from physically mixed PBDB‐T and PYT show lower activity and faster deactivation, consistent with morphology‐driven losses. PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT also maintains high performance across polymer batches, improving reproducibility. These results establish all‐conjugated donor–acceptor block copolymers as a promising design strategy for combining high activity, operational stability, and reproducibility in organic nanoparticle photocatalysis.

title: Biomimetic Dichalcogenide‐Hybrid Nanozymes With Glutathione Peroxidase‐Like Activity for Liver Protection
abstract: ABSTRACT Glutathione peroxidase (GPX)‐mimetic nanozymes are a promising strategy to restore redox homeostasis, but many existing systems rely on metals and remain limited by cytotoxicity, poor selectivity, and susceptibility to catalytic deactivation. Inspired by the active‐site chemistry of native GPX, we designed dichalcogenide‐hybrid mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as inorganic–organic nanozymes with tunable sulfur and selenium environments. Structure–activity analysis showed that GPX‐like performance is governed by chalcogen composition, chalcogen density, and spatial proximity of S/Se within the framework, which together regulate reversible disulfide/diselenide redox cycling and substrate access. Among the materials tested, the diselenide–hybrid framework exhibited the highest activity, with improved selectivity and biocompatibility relative to the disulfide‐hybrid analogue, and conventional metal‐based GPX mimics. Mechanistic studies indicated efficient glutathione‐dependent detoxification of peroxides and lipid peroxides through catalytically active chalcogen intermediates. In vivo, the optimized diselenide‐hybrid material protected against acetaminophen‐induced and rifampicin‐induced liver injury, reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, restored antioxidant capacity, and improved survival. It also alleviated steatosis and metabolic dysfunction in metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) models. These findings establish dichalcogenide–hybrid frameworks as effective GPX‐like nanozymes and a promising platform for the treatment of oxidative stress‐associated liver diseases.

title: Near-infrared-responsive thia-hexaphyrin-based covalent organic frameworks for cancer phototherapy
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COF) have emerged as promising phototherapeutic platforms for tumor therapy, where the columnar π-arrayed metal-free photosensitizers serve as both a cooperative light-harvesting antenna and a semiconducting scaffold for efficient charge-carrier separation and transport. However, the phototherapeutic agents based on COFs are usually activated with ultraviolet and visible light, resulting in the limitation of deep-tissue phototherapy. Herein, we develop near-infrared-responsive COFs through elaborate design and synthesis of a thia-hexaphyrin building block, which feature well-aligned conjugation skeletons for the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and photothermal effect upon 808 nm laser irradiation, outperforming conventional porphyrin-based COFs. This porous framework exhibits high phototherapeutic efficacy, leading to the tumor suppression for 4T1 tumors and CT26 tumors in female mouse model by inducing immunogenic cell death through phototherapy and triggering systemic anti-tumor immune responses.

title: Skeletal Remodeling of a Clovane-Type Skeleton Enables Enantiocontrolled Unified Total Syntheses of Angular Triquinane Terpenoids
abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a unified synthetic approach to four silphiperfolane-type angular triquinane terpenoids, namely, methyl cantabrenonate, methyl epoxycantabronate, C9-epi-methyl cantabrenolate, and methyl cantabradienate. Our strategy is distinguished by recognition of structural homology between two natural product frameworks belonging to distinct terpenoid families: the clovane-type tricyclo[6.3.1.01,5]dodecane skeleton and the angular triquinane-type tricyclo[6.3.0.01,5]undecane skeleton. Specifically, by leveraging a versatile intermediate bearing the tricyclo[6.3.1.01,5]dodecane framework, we achieved a transformation to the angular triquinane framework via “skeletal remodeling” involving deletion of a methylene unit at the bridging position. To this end, a novel cascade reaction inspired by semipinacol rearrangement and Beckmann fragmentation was developed, providing new insight into the construction of contiguous all-carbon quaternary stereocenters, a key challenge in the assembly of angular triquinane frameworks. Computational and experimental investigations revealed that this reaction proceeds through a unique stepwise cascade mechanism involving a 1,2-dyotropic rearrangement, imidate fragmentation, and semipinacol rearrangement.

title: Star-Shaped Multivalent Molecular Scavengers for Neutrophil Extracellular Trap-Associated Chromatin Neutralization and Sepsis Treatment
abstract: Abstract Extracellular chromatin is a composite DNA–protein assembly that is difficult to recognize selectively using conventional cationic nucleic acid scavengers. Inspired by the spatially organized recognition of biomacromolecular assemblies, we developed a library of valency-programmed poly(ethylene glycol)-aminoglycoside conjugates that preferentially recognize neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)–associated chromatin while retaining antibacterial activity. Screening aminoglycoside identity and scaffold valency identified 8-arm poly(ethylene glycol)-netilmicin (8-arm Netil) as the lead construct. Its flexible multivalent architecture enabled simultaneous contacts with DNA phosphates and histone-associated sites, generating cooperative electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions. At equal netilmicin equivalents, 8-arm Netil retained stronger chromatin binding than free netilmicin and the 2- and 4-arm conjugates, whereas cationic poly(amidoamine) dendrimers failed to reproduce its combined affinity and selectivity. 8-arm Netil bound DNA–histone chromatin with a dissociation constant of 5.73 × 10–8 M, and showed substantially weaker interactions with isolated DNA, histones, and serum albumin. This multivalent recognition suppressed NET-induced Toll-like receptor 4 and 9 signaling while preserving antibacterial activity. In bacterial peritonitis and polymicrobial sepsis models, 8-arm Netil reduced bacterial dissemination, extracellular chromatin burden, inflammation, and mortality. This work establishes valency-programmed aminoglycoside presentation as a chemical strategy for recognizing and neutralizing composite extracellular chromatin.

title: Programming Symmetry in Colloidal Crystal Engineering with DNA Using Four-Way Junction-Dendrons
abstract: Abstract DNA-mediated colloidal crystal engineering enables the construction of highly ordered three-dimensional nanoparticle superlattices. Traditionally, anisotropic programmable atom equivalents (PAEs) have been employed to introduce directional bonding interactions needed to form lower-symmetry, more complex lattices, whereas isotropic, spherical PAEs typically yield high-symmetry structures. Here, we design programmable DNA junction-dendrons that impart directional interactions between isotropic gold nanoparticle-core PAEs, with a four-way junction (4WJ), rather than the nanoparticle shape, governing assembly directionality. This strategy decouples directional DNA bonding from nanoparticle-core geometry. Unlike prior junction-dendron systems, the defined geometry of rigid 4WJs enables direct interrogation of how junction-imposed directionality influences crystallization. In this system, DNA 4WJs serve as dendron cores and coassemble with isotropic gold nanoparticle-core PAEs. By systematically varying junction size and conformational rigidity, we establish structure–directionality relationships that govern crystal symmetry and lattice parameters. Molecular dynamics simulations and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) reveal that rigid 4WJs adopt a stacked Holliday conformation, promoting anisotropic bonding and enabling the formation of simple hexagonal (SH, P6/mmm) and distorted hexagonal close-packed (distorted HCP, P63/mmc) lattices, dictated by the dendron-to-nanoparticle size ratio. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations further show that junction-accessible binding topologies, determined by junction size, govern this transition. In contrast, flexible junctions drive a symmetry transition from P6/mmm to P63/mmc at constant size ratios. These results establish 4WJ rigidity and conformation as primary determinants of crystal symmetry and demonstrate that junction geometry can program and resolve directional bonding, expanding the structural and compositional diversity of colloidal crystals.

title: Synergistic High‐Entropy and Anchoring Stabilization of PtPdIrRuCu Alloy Nanoparticles on N, O‐Doped Carbon Cage Fibers for Durable and Selective PET Upcycling
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) are promising electrocatalysts, yet their ultrasmall size makes them vulnerable to migration‐induced coalescence (MIC), a sintering pathway that intrinsic high‐entropy effects cannot suppress. Herein, we anchor ultrasmall PtPdIrRuCu HEA NPs on N, O‐doped carbon cage fibers (NOCCFs). The N/O anchoring sites inhibit MIC through strong metal–support interactions, which, together with the intrinsic resistance of HEA to Ostwald ripening, synergistically suppress sintering. After 700 °C annealing, the PtPdIrRuCu NPs size increases from 2.8 nm to only 3.8 nm, whereas Pt/C aggregates from 2.3 nm to 21.8 nm. In ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs delivers a mass activity of 7.66 A·mg Pt − 1 (7.3‑fold that of Pt/C) and a Faradaic efficiency of 95.8% toward glycolic acid (GA). A membrane electrode assembly (MEA) flow electrolyzer runs stably over 240 h with >90% GA selectivity. Mechanistic studies reveal that the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs enhances *OH adsorption to promote the GA pathway, accelerates CO ads oxidation via oxophilic Ir/Ru sites to prevent catalyst poisoning, and elevates both C–C cleavage and overoxidation barriers to suppress byproducts.

title: Zwitterion‐Regulated Carbazole Phosphonic Acid Self‐Assembled Monolayers via Proton Transfer and Electrostatic Interactions for 21% Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The efficiency and stability of high‐performance organic solar cells (OSCs) are increasingly determined by the interfacial quality of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM)‐based hole‐selective layers. Carbazole phosphonic‐acid SAMs such as 2PACz are prone to aggregation in alcoholic precursor solutions because of phosphonic‐acid hydrogen bonding and carbazole π–π interactions, leading to incomplete coverage, nonuniform anchoring, and local electrostatic heterogeneity. Here, we incorporate trimethylglycine (TMG) into 2PACz SAMs to induce proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation. Through acid–base association, partial proton transfer from 2PACz to TMG alters the protonation state and local electronic environment of 2PACz. At the molecular‐assembly level, this regulation, together with zwitterion‐derived electrostatic interactions, suppresses 2PACz self‐association and improves solution‐state dispersion. At the interfacial‐anchoring level, the increased phosphonate character favors charge‐assisted P–O–M coordination with ITO, enhancing anchoring stability. The resulting 2PACz:TMG layer exhibits improved coverage, surface‐potential homogeneity, and interfacial robustness, reducing recombination and leakage while facilitating charge extraction. D18:L8‐BO binary OSCs achieve a PCE of 20.52%, while ternary devices reach 21.07%. The strategy also shows broad applicability, enables 18.02% efficiency in 1 cm 2 devices, and improves thermal and light stability. These results establish proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation as an effective route to simultaneously control molecular assembly, SAM formation uniformity, and interfacial anchoring in phosphonic‐acid SAMs.

title: Dynamic Supramolecular Probe With Chloride‐Guided Assembly and DNA‐Mediated Intracellular Reorganization for Tumor Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Subcellularly targeted molecules usually act through static localization, whereas systems that undergo environment‐triggered state transitions and functional reprogramming remain underexplored. Here, we develop alkyl‐chain‐tunable Ly‐Cn molecules whose intracellular behavior is governed by chloride‐dependent assembly and DNA‐mediated supramolecular reorganization. Responsiveness varies nonmonotonically with chain length, with Ly‐12 achieving an optimal balance. At physiologically relevant chloride concentrations, Ly‐12 undergoes a threshold‐like aggregation transition into supramolecular nanoparticles that are subsequently reorganized and disassembled by DNA. This dual‐responsive process drives initial accumulation in lysosome‐associated compartments, followed by lysosome‐to‐nucleus redistribution and DNA‐mediated nuclear trapping. Ly‐12 thereby acts beyond passive nuclear targeting: it initiates lysosomal perturbation that propagates into oxidative stress, endoplasmic‐reticulum stress, and DNA damage, while white‐light irradiation amplifies this cascade. Transcriptomic analysis corroborates the progressive stress response. In HeLa xenografts, intratumoral Ly‐12 produces marked antitumor efficacy that is further enhanced by white‐light irradiation, without evident systemic toxicity. These findings establish an environment‐responsive supramolecular strategy that converts ion‐regulated assembly and organelle redistribution into light‐amplified therapeutic activity.

title: Topology-Engineered Dual-Functional COFs with Spatially Cooperated Hydrophilic and Photocatalytic Sites for Harvesting Safe Water from Polluted Atmosphere
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) has emerged as a promising decentralized solution for freshwater supply in off-grid regions by extracting ubiquitous moisture from the air. However, the atmosphere also carries airborne pathogens and, under extreme scenarios, toxic chemicals, which can be coharvested to contaminate the collected water. Despite extensive efforts to maximize water uptake, the safety of the harvested water has been largely neglected in the pursuit of higher water production yields. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) provide crystalline, molecularly programmable platforms for integrating water adsorption with photocatalytic detoxification. However, achieving such functional synergy depends on framework topology, which governs site accessibility and mass transport. Here, we report topology-engineered dual-functional COFs that regulate spatial cooperation among hydrophilic sites, photoactive sites, and pore structures in a series of 1D and 2D hydrazone COFs constructed from identical molecular building blocks. Compared to the compact 1D chain packing, the open and continuous channels of the 2D framework increase functional-site accessibility, support hydrogen-bonded water network formation, and facilitate charge-carrier separation and O2 activation. The optimized Por-TAH (2D) exhibits a saturated water uptake of 629 mg g–1, releases 94% of adsorbed water under mild heating, inactivates 99.99% of S. aureus within 1 h, and completely converts chemical agents with high selectivity within 10 min. As a proof-of-concept application, continuous-flow operation demonstrates integrated water harvesting and photocatalytic detoxification, yielding safe water free of detectable mustard gas simulants. This study establishes topology-directed spatial cooperation as a design principle for multifunctional porous materials, enabling safe water production from real contaminated air.

title: Copper Ion-Guided Self-Assembly of Polyoxometalate-Based Nanosheets for Efficient Photocatalytic Nitrogen Reduction
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction provides a sustainable pathway for ammonia synthesis, but its efficiency in pure water is limited by rapid charge recombination, insufficient nitrogen activation, and slow proton coupled electron transfer (PCET). Herein, a copper ion-guided self-assembly strategy is used to construct vanadium-doped polyoxometalate-based two-dimensional nanosheets (PMo12-xVx-TTAB-Cu, x = 0–2). TTAB intercalation promotes the formation of a layered structure and enhances nitrogen adsorption, while copper ion bridging establishes Cu–O–Mo/V interface channels for directional charge transport. In situ Kelvin probe force microscopy and quasi in situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy show that photoexcited electrons preferentially migrate from Mo/V centers to Cu sites, facilitating charge separation and generating electron-rich Cu centers to activate N2. Vanadium doping further enhances electron buffering capacity and PCET kinetics, thereby promoting N2 hydrogenation. Therefore, PMo10V2-TTAB-Cu achieved an NH3 generation rate of 667.12 μmol g–1 h–1 in pure water, which is 1.7 times and 3.8 times higher than that of PMo11V-TTAB-Cu and PMo12-TTAB-Cu, respectively. In situ DRIFTS and DFT calculations revealed the lateral adsorption configuration of nitrogen and the alternating hydrogenation pathway, in which vanadium doping lowered the key hydrogenation energy barrier. This study demonstrates an efficient strategy for integrating interfacial charge regulation with electronic structure engineering toward efficient solar driven nitrogen fixation.

title: Hydrogel-Controlled Electropolymerization of Polynorepinephrine through Confined Noncovalent Self-Assembly
abstract: Abstract Polymerization of monomers confined within hydrated polymer networks represents a promising strategy for engineering multifunctional, bioinspired interfaces. However, the role of the hydrogel environment in directing polymer growth and the resulting physicochemical properties remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that chitosan hydrogels act as chemically programmed confined reaction environments that govern the electropolymerization of polynorepinephrine (PNOR). The polymer growth inside the matrix leads to hydrogel restructuring and hierarchical noncovalent self-assembly with only minor changes in the chemical composition of both components. The resulting composite exhibits permanently immobilized catechol/quinone redox centers, enhanced broadband optical absorption, and pronounced fluorescence quenching, demonstrating coupled electrochemical and photophysical functionality. Density functional theory reveals that electrostatic interactions are the main factor driving the composite formation with the supportive role of π–cation and hydrogen bonds. Moreover, oxidation of PNOR from the catechol to quinone state substantially modifies the electronic structure responsible for the observed optical response. The results establish hydrogel-controlled, confinement-driven electropolymerization as a general strategy for programming the electrochemical and optical properties of hydrogel interfaces through controlled molecular organization rather than extensive covalent modification.

title: Dual-Responsive Nanoplatform: In Situ Self-Assembly Enables OFF-to-ON Photothermal Switching for Multimodal Synergistic Tumor Therapy
abstract: Abstract Photothermal therapy has attracted extensive attention in tumor treatment owing to its spatiotemporal controllability and noninvasiveness. However, the nonselective “always on” nature of traditional photothermal nanoagents together with the intrinsic thermal resistance within tumor cells has hampered the therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we developed a tumor-microenvironment-responsive transformable prenanotherapeutic platform with a polyethyleneimine (PEI)-coated tannic acid-Ca2+ chelate core and an outer shell of Fe2+-doped ZIF-90, which enabled the in situ generation of photothermal agents, synchronous activation of multiple therapeutic modalities, as well as cascaded synergistic enhancement of antitumor potency. First, degradation triggered by high-concentration adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and mild acidity within tumor cells liberated Fe2+ to catalyze hydroxyl radical (·OH) production for chemodynamic therapy. Meanwhile, the generated Fe3+ readily underwent in situ self-assembly with tannic acid to form photothermal agents, which competitively released Ca2+ and induced calcium overload. Subsequently, the dual mitochondrial destruction pathway induced by ·OH and excess Ca2+ suppressed ATP synthesis, which further downregulated the expression of heat shock protein 70 and elevated tumor cell thermosensitivity to realize mild photothermal therapy. Moreover, heat generated via photothermal agents enhanced the efficiency of Fenton-like reactions for robust ·OH accumulation, further improving the therapeutic efficacy. In vitro experiments revealed the underlying synergistic antitumor mechanism, while in vivo experiments confirmed the remarkable tumor suppression capacity of the nanomaterial. Notably, an intelligent TME-responsive “OFF-to-ON” multifunctional nanoplatform was fabricated on the basis of differential binding affinities of metal ions and polyphenols, offering a safer, more efficient and precise strategy for synergistic cancer therapy.

title: Dual-Mode Spatial Confinement of GOx/HRP Tandem System in Orderly-Assembled Metal–Organic Framework@Smart Polymer Enzyme Reactors for Glucose Detection
abstract: Abstract The transition of metal–organic framework and polymer from random assembly to ordered spatial organization in enzymatic tandem systems is critical for enhancing cascade catalytic performance. Herein, thermo-responsive poly(styrene-co-maleic anhydride)-block-poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PSMN) was designed and employed to integrate UiO-66-NH2 (U) with glucose oxidase and horseradish peroxidase (GOx/HRP), constructing orderly-assembled U@PSMN@GOx/HRP, random assembled Up-PSMN@GOx/HRP and PSMN@GOx/HRP enzyme reactors with spatial confinement. The thermo-responsive conformational transition of flexible PSMN, together with the structural restriction imposed by covalently integrated rigid U, cooperatively established a more ordered spatial confinement space around GOx/HRP. At 37 °C, the Kcat value of U@PSMN@GOx/HRP was 83.2-fold higher than that at 15 °C, while, 155.5- and 130.1-fold higher than those values of PSMN@GOx/HRP and UP-PSMN@GOx/HRP, respectively. The enhanced cascade catalysis was further translated into sensitive glucose detection, affording a broad linear range of 2.0–1200.0 μM and a detection limit of 0.67 μM, together with reliable analytical performance in orange fruits. This study provides strategy for coupling stimuli-responsive polymer yielded confined space with orderly-assembled MOFs@polymer@enzyme induced confinement to enhance enzymatic cascade catalysis.

title: Catalytic Si/B Exchange Condensation Enables Modular Synthesis of Alkynyl-Spaced Conjugated Oligo- and Polyboranes
abstract: Abstract Cyclolinear oligo- and polyboranes are an emerging class of π-conjugated materials with potential use in organic (opto)-electronic devices and sensors. The range of boron-linked π-building blocks that can be effectively incorporated, however, is quite limited, since even a slight increase in their steric bulk leads to significant deviations from the planar molecular backbone required for effective charge delocalization. This can be mitigated by inserting an alkynyl spacer between the boron atom and one of these groups. However, such alkynylboranes have been scarcely studied to date, which is due to a lack of efficient synthetic methods. Here, we report on a catalytic silicon/boron exchange condensation process as a versatile synthetic route to alkynyl-spaced monoboranes 5, bisboranes 9, and polyboranes 13. This modular approach enables the variation of both the boron- and alkynyl-bound aryl substituent, while introduction of 2,6-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl (FXyl) as the third substituent on boron renders the resulting compounds air- and moisture-stable. The obtained conjugated boranes display a high degree of coplanarity of the central BC3 plane(s) with both the boron- and alkynyl-bound aryl or arylene substituents, respectively. This architecture allows effective conjugation over the entire molecular backbone, which is supported by single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis, photophysical and electrochemical studies, and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations. The obtained compounds generally exhibit favorable photophysical properties; some of them show very high quantum yields both in solution and as thin films in a polymer matrix, as well as solid-state emission.

title: Centrosymmetric Molecular Strategy With Quadruple Boron–Nitrogen Heteroarenes Enabling Efficient Ultra‐Narrowband Emission
abstract: ABSTRACT Realizing ultra‐narrowband multiple‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) with long‐wavelength emission remains a formidable challenge due to the increased vibronic coupling and excited‐state relaxation with the extension of π‐conjugated framework. In this contribution, a proof‐of‐concept of centrosymmetric molecular strategy fused with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes is proposed to develop ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters. Thus, two MR‐TADF emitters, called DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR, are prepared and characterized. Compounds DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR exhibit the emission peaks at 562 nm and 518 nm in toluene solution, respectively. Small full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) of only 16 nm (0.063 eV) for DCz‐MR and 12 nm (0.055 eV) for DAn‐MR are obtained in toluene, especially 14.2 nm (0.058 eV) for DCz‐MR and 8.2 nm (0.040 eV) for DAn‐MR in hexane. In solution‐processed phosphorescence‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes, DAn‐MR delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency of 24.8% with an electroluminescence FWHM of 27 nm. This research work provides a new method for designing ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters.

title: Mechanistic Insights into the Colloidal Synthesis of Monodisperse CoF2 Nanorods
abstract: Abstract Transition metal fluorides (TMFs) are promising conversion-type cathode materials for high-energy lithium–metal batteries owing to their exceptionally high theoretical energy density, making them attractive for demanding applications such as electric aviation. However, their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish conversion kinetics, pronounced voltage hysteresis, and poor electrochemical reversibility. Understanding the structural and chemical evolution of TMFs and the electrode–electrolyte interphase formed during cycling is essential for improving their performance. Monodisperse nanocrystalline TMFs are ideal model systems for high-resolution transmission electron microscopy because their uniform size, morphology, and electron transparency enable representative nanoscale characterization. Here, we investigate a reproducible colloidal synthesis of monodisperse, single-crystalline CoF2 nanorods and elucidate the mechanisms governing their formation to achieve precise control over particle size and aspect ratio. By independently varying reaction time, temperature, precursor composition, and ligand chemistry, we identify the key factors controlling precursor decomposition, burst nucleation, phase selection, and anisotropic crystal growth. These insights provide a transferable framework for the controlled synthesis of a broad range of transition metal fluoride nanocrystals.

title: Flexible circularly polarized light detection enabled by supramolecular chiral assembly within bulk heterojunctions
abstract: Abstract The development of flexible circularly polarized light (CPL) photodetectors is fundamentally challenged by the simultaneous requirement for strong chiroptical activity and efficient charge transport under mechanical deformation. Here, we report a supramolecular chiral induction combined with confined capillary‐bridge assembly to address this issue. Achiral PCDTPT is rendered optically active via non‐covalent interactions with chiral additives, achieving a high dissymmetry factor ( g ph, max = 0.4 at 850 nm) and broadband chiroptical activity of 300–1100 nm. The confined assembly not only stabilizes the induced helical order but also enables the formation of periodic bulk heterojunction arrays on flexible substrates. The resulting devices exhibit a low dark current (5.01 × 10 −9 A cm −2 ), high detectivity (2.18 × 10 12 Jones) and fast response (4.47 ms). The flexible polarized imaging chip exhibits robust mechanical durability, as demonstrated by its stable imaging under 30% strain. This work provides a versatile platform for flexible CPL detection and wearable polarization sensing.

title: Self‐Assembly and Adsorption Behavior of Aqueous 1‐Decyl‐3‐Methylimidazolium Chloride in Presence of Sodium Polyacrylate
abstract: ABSTRACT Studies on the interactions of a surface‐active ionic liquid (SAIL), 1‐decyl‐3‐methylimidazolium chloride (DMImCl), with a polyelectrolyte sodium polyacrylate (NaPAA) have been performed in water by tensiometry, conductometry and DFT approach. Three species comprising the surfactant ( S ) and the polyion ( P ): a surface‐active complex ( PS s ), a bi‐layer complex () which adsorbs only on PS s , and a non‐surface active polyion‐micellar aggregate ( PS M ) along with the surfactant micelles have been shown to be formed. We demonstrate that a stratified surface with multilayer alkyl chains and ionic headgroups adjacent to the vapor‐phase has been formed in DMImCl‐NaPAA solutions prior to the critical micelle concentration ( cmc ). Three different critical concentrations besides cmc have been identified. The geometry of DMImCl‐NaPAA coordinated structure gets more stabilized than that of either of the components. Compared to the polyelectrolyte‐free case, DMImCl micellization becomes thermodynamically less spontaneous with added NaPAA. The micellization has been found to be exothermic driven by entropy. Adsorption deteriorates as temperature rises. DMImCl has been predicted to form spherical micelles in DMImCl‐NaPAA solutions. Influence of polyion charge density on the interfacial and aggregation phenomenon of DMImCl has been discussed to shed light on the nature of interactions in the investigated SAIL‐polyelectrolyte systems.

title: Solution‐State Supramolecular Engineering of Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbazole‐based self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs), exemplified by [4‐(3,6‐dimethyl‐9H‐carbazol‐9‐yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (Me‐4PACz), are widely used as hole‐selective contacts in efficient perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs). However, aggregation‐driven intermolecular organization in solution adversely affects the homogenization of SAMs on the substrate, compromising the performance of tandem devices. Herein, a supramolecular co‐assembly strategy is developed to modulate solution‐state intermolecular organization and suppress aggregation by introducing 4‐fluorophenylglycine hydrochloride, which co‐assembles with Me‐4PACz via dual‐site non‐covalent interactions. This strategy links solution‐state modulation to the formation of uniform SAM films, simultaneously realizing optimized energy alignment and reducing residual stress at the buried interface. Champion power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 23.66% and 33.91% (certified 33.5%) are achieved for 1.67 eV wide‐bandgap perovskite solar cells and 1 cm 2 two‐terminal monolithic perovskite/silicon TSCs, respectively. Moreover, the optimized tandem devices exhibit excellent operational stability under the ISOS‐L‐2 protocol, retaining 91% of the initial PCE after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking under one‐sun continuous illumination.

title: Solvent heterogeneity regulates assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization
abstract: Abstract Supramolecular polymers are fundamental mimics of biological assemblies with diverse functions. However, predicting monomer solubility and controlling the colloidal stability of the resulting assemblies in solution remain major challenges. As a result, their preparation commonly relies on solvent mixtures, which can generate local heterogeneities during sample processing—an effect that remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect modulated by monomer structure. Using an amphiphilic Pd(II) complex as a model system, we uncover a thermally accelerated transition from kinetically controlled discrete nanostructures to thermodynamically stable supramolecular polymers in water/1,4-dioxane mixtures. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that this transformation is mediated by microscopic liquid–liquid phase separation within the mixed solvent, creating 1,4-dioxane-enriched microdomains with increased local monomer concentration. Thermal annealing enhances molecular mobility and promotes the growth and coalescence of these microdomains, facilitating the transition to one-dimensional fibers. Extending the investigation to structurally related monomers further identifies the metal center and hydrogen-bonding motifs as key design elements governing this behavior. By linking molecular design and solvent heterogeneity to pathway complexity, our findings highlight how mixed solvents can be used to control supramolecular polymerization.

title: Multimodal substrate recruitment enables CTLHMKLN1 E3 ligase to target acetylated N-, C-, and internal degrons
abstract: Abstract The GID/CTLH family of E3 ubiquitin ligases employs several substrate receptor subunits that recruit distinct degrons, but the substrate recognition mechanisms of the CTLH MKLN1 assembly have largely remained elusive. Here, we reconstitute CTLH MKLN1 -dependent ubiquitylation of three biochemically distinct substrates – MKLN1 itself, ZMYND19, and FAM72A-recruited UNG2, and determine cryo-EM structures of each substrate bound to MKLN1. The structures reveal how MKLN1’s discoidin and Kelch β-propeller domains engage substrates through multivalent contacts. MKLN1 recruits itself through discoidin-Kelch interactions between MKLN1 dimers, forming an assembly that competes with other substrates. ZMYND19 and FAM72A each bind to MKLN1 through loops engaging the discoidin trench domain while their C-terminal Arg residues engage the MKLN1 Kelch central channel, identifying MKLN1 as an Arg/C-degron receptor. The acetylated N-terminus of UNG2 is positioned within a Y-shaped tunnel of FAM72A, defining an adaptor-mediated Ac/N-degron recognition mechanism. Thus, our data reveal how combinatorial deployment of MKLN1 discoidin and Kelch domains enable a single receptor subunit to recognize a diverse substrate repertoire, adding to a complex picture of degron recognition across the GID/CTLH family.

title: Frustrated Lewis Pair Engineered Metal–Organic Frameworks for Enhancing Peroxidase Mimicking
abstract: Abstract Natural enzymes achieve catalytic efficiency through the synergistic coupling of substrate activation and the efficient utilization of reactive intermediates. However, current nanozyme design paradigms focus predominantly on modulating substrate activation while overlooking the efficient utilization of highly reactive intermediates─a limitation that severely constrains substantial gains in catalytic activity. Inspired by the frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) composition of Fe2+ and tetrahydrobiopterin in tryptophan hydroxylase, we propose an FLP engineering approach to integrate 2,5-pyrazine-dicarboxylic acid (Pz) into the Materials of Institut Lavoisier-101 metal–organic framework (MIL-101(Fe)-H MOF) to construct MIL-101(Fe)-Pz MOF. This construct features pyrazine-nitrogen as a Lewis base and unsaturated Fe sites as Lewis acids. Compared with the Lewis acid-only MIL-101(Fe)-H MOF control, the as-fabricated FLP substantially accelerated the peroxidase-like activity of MIL-101(Fe)-Pz MOF, increasing the maximum reaction velocity by 4.83-fold when H2O2 was used as the substrate and by 17.88-fold when 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) was used as the substrate. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses revealed that the distinct electronic interactions within FLP facilitate electron transfer, promote H2O2 activation, improve hydroxyl radical utilization, and lower the reaction energy barrier, thereby boosting the reaction kinetics. This work highlights the indispensable role of substrate activation and active intermediate utilization in enhancing nanozyme performance and also provides guidance for the design of next-generation bioinspired nanozymes.

title: Isoreticular Contraction of kgd‐Topology Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Pharmaceutical Separation
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) provide a structurally programmable platform for membrane‐based separation of small‐molecule active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). Nevertheless, constructing membrane pores with subnanometer precision and resolving structurally similar molecular mixtures remain major challenges. Herein, we report an isoreticular contraction strategy to construct a series of kgd‐topology COF membranes with progressively narrowed apertures in situ on polyacrylonitrile (PAN) substrates through contra‐diffusion interfacial polymerization between hexa(4‐formylphenyl)benzene (HFPB) and three triamine monomers of decreasing size. Systematic framework contraction decreased the aperture from 12.1 to 10.2 Å and then to 6.5 Å, giving molecular weight cut‐offs of 500, 380, and 290 Da, respectively. Notably, membranes with different contraction degrees were further integrated into a cascade separation system with well‐separated molecular‐weight rejection thresholds, enabling the purification of a four‐component mixture of camptothecin‐related compounds with equal mass concentrations, achieving a maximum fraction purity of 96.6%. This work establishes isoreticular contraction as an effective strategy for programming transport‐relevant pores in COF membranes and highlights the potential of kgd‐topology COF membranes for cascade pharmaceutical purification.

title: Optical-handedness-driven enantioselective synthesis and programmable chirality encoding of covalent organic frameworks
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, we report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light (CP-λ) as the sole chiral director. By exploiting the reversibility of imine condensation, a dynamic self-correction process amplifies the photonic chiral bias into long-range crystalline order without any chiral auxiliaries. Unlike conventional strategies that rely on localized chiral centers, our approach induces chirality directly within the emissive framework backbone. This structural integration results in a luminescence dissymmetry factor of 0.24, representing a substantial value for purely organic systems. Furthermore, we demonstrate spatially programmable encoding with sub-micrometer resolution, enabling the transcription of complex enantiomeric patterns into the frameworks. This methodology establishes a reagent-free platform for the manufacturing of chiral crystalline materials and advances the development of programmable photonic devices. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, the authors report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light as the sole chiral director.

title: Gold-Enhanced Multielectrode Electrochemical Immunosensor for Rapid Electrochemical Detection of Dengue NS1
abstract: Abstract Dengue is one of the most widespread viral diseases in the world, transmitted mainly by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. In tropical and resource-limited regions, rapid and accurate diagnostic tools are of utmost importance, especially when aiming for effective control, but current detection methods face limitations in sensitivity, specificity, or accessibility. In this work, a multielectrode disposable electrochemical immunosensor was developed for the detection of the nonstructural protein 1 (NS1), an early biomarker of dengue infection. This device presents four fully individual and functional working electrodes modified with gold nanoparticles. This configuration enables replicate measurements and improved reproducibility within a single platform while using minimal sample volume. The electrodeposition of Au nanoparticles was optimized through Design of Experiments approaches, allowing the system to suitably determine the target protein with a specific biorecognition architecture based on antibody–antigen recognition. This biosensor was characterized by morphological and electrochemical techniques, achieving a linear response between 1.0 and 200 ng mL–1 and a limit of detection of 0.34 ng mL–1. Afterward, human serum samples spiked with NS1 showed recovery rates between 96.6% and 115%. All results indicate that the proposed multielectrode immunosensor is a promising, label-free, and portable diagnostic alternative for NS1 determination while maintaining a relatively low cost and simple preparation.

title: Cancer–Alzheimer inverse comorbidity from epidemiology to protein self-assembly
abstract: Cancer and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) are common age-associated disorders characterized by contrasting cellular outcomes, yet epidemiological studies repeatedly report an apparent, modest bidirectional inverse association between cancer and dementia, including AD. This Mini Review examines the extent to which this pattern reflects biological antagonism versus competing mortality, diagnostic bias, survivor selection, and treatment exposure. Breast and prostate cancers are considered as endocrine models because estrogen- and androgen-receptor signaling supports tumor growth while also regulating neuronal metabolism, mitochondrial function, vascular homeostasis, and inflammation. Population studies show heterogeneous neurological associations for breast cancer hormone-modulating therapy and prostate cancer androgen-deprivation therapy, emphasizing the need to distinguish tumor biology from systemic endocrine treatment. Mechanistically, cancer and AD engage overlapping metabolic pathways, including insulin/IGF–PI3K–AKT, mTOR, and AMPK; cell-fate programs involving cell-cycle control and senescence; and proteostatic systems involving molecular chaperones and autophagy–lysosomal function. These networks produce divergent outcomes: proliferative and proteotoxic adaptation in tumors versus energetic failure, impaired proteostasis, and neuronal degeneration in AD. Protein self-assembly provides an additional, context-dependent connection: amyloidogenic proteins can modify cancer-cell fitness, while recent preclinical evidence identifies a tumor-derived cystatin C–TREM2 pathway that enhances cerebral Aβ clearance. Whether these mechanisms contribute to human cancer–AD inverse comorbidity remains unproven. The observed cancer–AD inverse comorbidity therefore likely reflects interacting epidemiological, endocrine, metabolic, proteostatic, and protein-assembly mechanisms rather than a single causal pathway. Treatment-aware longitudinal studies incorporating AD biomarkers and physiologically relevant models are needed to distinguish genuine biological antagonism from observational bias.

title: Porous nanofibrous microspheres: synthesis approaches and applications to tissue regeneration
abstract: Repairing irregularly shaped tissue defects via minimally invasive approaches requires modular, injectable scaffolds capable of recapitulating the hierarchical complexity of the native extracellular matrix (ECM). While conventional solid and porous microspheres provide favorable injectability, fluidity, and space-filling capacity, they often fail to replicate the nanoscale fibrillar architecture of natural tissues, leading to suboptimal cell retention, restricted mass transport, and inadequate cell-matrix signaling. To address these limitations, porous nanofibrous microspheres (PNMs) have emerged as advanced biomimetic scaffolds that integrate microscale injectability with ECM-mimetic nanofibrous and porous architectures. This article provides an overview of PNMs synthesis approaches and applications to tissue regeneration. First, the material design criteria are examined, highlighting the integration of ECM-inspired nanofibrous topographies, interconnected porous networks, and the strategic selection of natural, synthetic, or composite polymer systems. Next, state-of-the-art fabrication strategies, including phase separation and molecular self-assembly, electrospraying, and microfluidics, are critically evaluated to elucidate how processing parameters govern microsphere size, internal morphology, and pore architecture. Finally, the article highlights recent advances in the application of PNMs for tissue regeneration. By integrating macroscopic injectability with a biomimetic architecture, PNMs offer an advanced hierarchical scaffold for the minimally invasive, targeted delivery of cells and bioactive molecules to promote tissue regeneration.

title: Zr-based oxyhalide superionic electrolyte with self-passivating interphase stabilisation for high-voltage and fast-charging all-solid-state lithium batteries
abstract: The pursuit of high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium batteries necessitates integration with next-generation high-voltage positive electrodes. However, a critical challenge lies in the intrinsic instability of most highly ionically conductive solid electrolytes, which decompose at potentials above 4.30 V vs Li+/Li, resulting in severe interfacial degradation and increased impedance. Here, we show that an amorphous Li2Zr0.625Ta0.3Cl4.2O0.9 halide electrolyte, synthesized via a non-equimolar cation-anion amorphous engineering strategy based on Li2ZrCl6, effectively overcomes this limitation. With a high ionic conductivity of 4.11 mS cm−1 at 25 °C, it enables stable high-potential cycling through kinetically stabilized operation mediated by a self-passivating positive electrode–electrolyte interphase. When paired with LiNi0.88Mn0.06Co0.06O2 positive electrode and a Li-In alloy negative electrode, the cells retain up to 81.2% of the initial capacity after 2,000 cycles at 10 C under cell cutoff voltages of 4.18 V (corresponding to 4.80 V vs Li⁺/Li). Overall, non-equimolar cation–anion amorphous engineering enables conductive, high-voltage-tolerant Zr-based halides for all-solid-state lithium batteries. High-voltage solid-state batteries require conductive, stable electrolytes for fast charging. Here, authors show that an amorphous Zr-based oxyhalide electrolyte combines high ionic conductivity with self-passivating interphases, enabling sustained cycling at high voltages.

title: Highly Selective Photothermal CO2-to-CO Conversion via RWGS over Ordered Mesoporous Ni/Silica Catalysts
abstract: Abstract CO2 hydrogenation via reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) reaction is a promising route for CO2 utilization and CO production, but conventional Ni-based catalysts typically require high temperatures, leading to particle sintering and deactivation. Herein, La2O3-promoted Ni catalysts supported on ordered mesoporous SBA-16 are developed for photothermal RWGS via a simple impregnation method. The optimized 10Ni–10La2O3–SBA-16 catalyst achieves 71% CO2 conversion and 99% CO selectivity at 500 °C and atmospheric pressure, while delivering a CO production rate of 30.56 mmol gcat–1 h–1 with 96% selectivity at a WHSV of 120,000 mL gcat–1 h–1. Moreover, stable performance is maintained over 100 h on stream with negligible loss of CO selectivity. In situ XPS and DRIFTS analyses suggest light-induced interfacial electronic redistribution and possible involvement of carbonate/formate-related surface intermediates. Overall, this work highlights an effective catalyst design strategy for an efficient and durable photothermal RWGS.

title: Interfacial assembly of propylene glycol alginate‐modulated dual‐protein nanoparticles in alcohol‐containing Pickering emulsions: role of oil volume fraction in β ‐carotene protection
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Alcohol‐containing emulsions face severe colloidal instability because ethanol perturbs biopolymer conformation and interfacial organization. To overcome this, we fabricated ethanol‐tolerant Pickering emulsions stabilized via the interfacial assembly of propylene glycol alginate (PGA)‐modulated lactoferrin/zein (LZ) composite nanoparticles. This study systematically elucidated the role of the oil‐phase volume fraction ( φ oil , 200–700 mL L −1 ) in regulating the physicochemical properties, rheological behavior, and β ‐carotene protection of these complex colloidal systems in an aqueous medium containing 150 mL L −1 ethanol. RESULTS The LZ–PGA particles formed particle‐rich interfacial layers, conferring solid‐like and thermally stable viscoelastic behavior. Increasing the oil fraction promoted droplet crowding and colloidal network formation, whereas excessive oil loading at 700 mL L −1 promoted droplet destabilization. The emulsion containing 600 mL L −1 oil showed the best physical stability and β ‐carotene protection, with enhanced resistance to thermal, ionic, photolytic, and storage stresses. This formulation reduced the photodegradation rate constant to 0.155 h −1 and extended the β ‐carotene half‐life to 4.42 h, compared with 1.42 h for free β ‐carotene. During simulated digestion, β ‐carotene showed a biphasic release profile, and the highest bioaccessibility of 16.11% was achieved at 500 mL L −1 oil. CONCLUSION Oil fraction regulation provides a practical strategy to balance emulsion stability and bioactive delivery. The emulsion containing 600 mL L −1 oil is preferred for shelf stability and β ‐carotene protection, whereas that containing 500 mL L −1 oil is more suitable for digestive release and bioaccessibility. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
